title: Completeness of restricted-series quotients over a rank-one valuation ring
statement: Let $K$ be a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial rank-one absolute value, and let $V=\{a\in K:|a|\leq1\}$ be its valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Choose $\pi\in V$ with $0<|\pi|<1$. For $r\geq0$, let $V\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$ denote the ring of power series with coefficients in $V$ tending to zero. For every ideal $J$ in this ring put $A=V\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle/J$. Then $A$ is separated and complete for the $\pi$-adic topology: the natural map $A\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/\pi^nA$ is an isomorphism. The valuation need not be discrete, and neither finite generation of $J$ nor torsion-freeness of $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Section 2.3, Corollary 9, printed p. 132, following Proposition 8; case (V) is an adic valuation ring with principal ideal of definition (section 2.3 opening, printed p. 129). Primary PDF read online, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $S=V\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$ and $D=K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$. By [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion], $D$ is complete for $\|f\|=\sup_\nu|f_\nu|$. The subring $S$ is its closed unit ball: a limit of series with coefficients of absolute value at most $1$ has the same property, since each coefficient difference is bounded by the Gauss distance. Hence every Cauchy sequence in $S$ has a limit in $S$. Moreover $\pi^n S=\{f\in S:\|f\|\le |\pi|^n\}$: division of every coefficient by $\pi^n$ preserves restrictedness and gives coefficients in $V$ precisely under this bound. These sets are closed. As $|\pi|^n\to0$, their translates form the Gauss neighbourhood basis on $S$, and their intersection is zero.

source.place: Section 2.3 opening, printed p. 129: restricted series as the adic completion of the polynomial ring; explicit unit-ball deduction from the existing Gauss-completeness node.

proof.text: Let $x\in\bigcap_{n\ge1}\pi^n A$. The $S$-module $A=S/J$ is generated by the image of $1$. Apply [lem-trf-restricted-submodule-adic-topology] with $M=A$, $N=Sx$, and $m=1$. For its resulting $n\ge1$, $x\in\pi^n A\cap Sx\subseteq\pi Sx$, so $x=\pi b x$ for some $b\in S$. The series $u=\sum_{k\ge0}(\pi b)^k$ converges in $S$ by step 1: every finite tail starting at $k$ has norm at most $|\pi|^k$. Multiplication is continuous by the Gauss product bound, and $(1-\pi b)\sum_{k=0}^N(\pi b)^k=1-(\pi b)^{N+1}\to1$, so $(1-\pi b)u=1$. Since $(1-\pi b)x=0$, this gives $x=0$. This proves injectivity of the natural completion map, with no torsion-freeness assumption on $A$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Proposition 8, printed p. 132: cyclic submodule of an infinitely divisible element and the geometric-series inverse; the topology comparison is Lemma 7(ii).

proof.text: For surjectivity, let $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ be compatible residues in $A/\pi^n A$, and write $q:S\to A$. Construct $f_n\in S$ with $q(f_n)\bmod\pi^n A=a_n$ and $f_{n+1}-f_n\in\pi^n S$. Choose $f_1$ by surjectivity of the quotient maps. Having chosen $f_n$, choose $g\in S$ representing $a_{n+1}$. Compatibility gives $q(g-f_n)\in\pi^n A$, so $g-f_n=j+\pi^n h$ for $j\in J$, $h\in S$: lift the element of $A$ multiplying $\pi^n$ and subtract its lift. Set $f_{n+1}=g-j$. It represents $a_{n+1}$ and has the required difference. Finite telescoping shows $f_k-f_n\in\pi^n S$ for $k\ge n$, so step 1 gives a limit $f\in S$. Closedness of $\pi^n S$ gives $f-f_n\in\pi^n S$, whence $q(f)$ represents every $a_n$. The canonical map is therefore surjective as well as injective. Its operations are componentwise by [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], so this bijective ring homomorphism is an isomorphism.

source.place: Section 2.3, Proposition 8 and Corollary 9, printed p. 132: explicit recursive lifting argument for completeness of the quotient, followed by the inverse-limit definition (Stacks 0317, definition-complete).

from.place: Historical analytic input supporting the normalization chain from lem-trf-local-term-locality, through Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2: Completeness of restricted-series quotients over a rank-one valuation ring. This is below the node level, not a replacement of the current contracting-correspondence unit proof.

split_report.summary: Statement retained, including arbitrary J and nondiscrete valuation. Reused existing Gauss completeness; separatedness follows from the induced topology on a cyclic submodule and an explicit geometric inverse. Recursive representatives prove surjectivity. The single new statement-only node is the independent submodule-topology theorem, Bosch 2.3/7(ii), not a completeness clause. Added the existing definitions of restricted series and adic completion.
split_report.blueprint: Historical analytic support for the normalization chain below lem-trf-local-term-locality, via Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2 and the parent Grauert-Remmert argument. The latest blueprint local-term proof uses contracting correspondences; this delivery only resolves the historical analytic prerequisite and changes neither the unit nor its route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q153-9321f70c2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the cited source online because there is no local copy (Bosch heft378 §2.3, pp.129-132; text via pdftotext). Lemma 7(ii) states that for any submodule N of a finite A-module M, the I-adic topology of M restricts to the I-adic topology on N; Prop 8 and Cor 9 are the item's source. The item statement is identical to the base. The base item was unsplit with no proof and no repair note, so this is not a re-split. Step 1: S is the closed unit ball of the complete Gauss norm from lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion, and pi^nS={||f||<=|pi|^n} are closed; elementary. Step 2 is Bosch's Prop 8 argument: apply the new node to M=A, N=Sx, m=1 to get x=pi*b*x; 1-pi*b is a unit of S by the geometric series, so x=0. Bosch writes 'unit in R'; the step correctly says S. Step 3: recursive lifts f_{n+1}=g-j with f_{n+1}-f_n in pi^nS give a Cauchy sequence whose limit lies in S by closedness of pi^nS; it does not need J closed. The new node lem-trf-restricted-submodule-adic-topology is Lemma 7(ii) specialized to A=V<T>, keeping arbitrary finite M and arbitrary N. I checked it independently: the torsion of M/N is finitely generated by Raynaud-Gruson, so it is killed by some pi^c and n=m+c works. It also holds in the r=0 small cases: ideal N (principal, non-principal or 0) and M=V/aV. It is a strictly smaller topology comparison, not a clause of the item. It is statement-only and self-contained, cites definition nodes for every notion, records leansearch, loogle, leanfinder and grep searches, and has correct blueprint from/via. An rg -L duplicate search over the restricted-series, Tate-algebra and Artin-Rees nodes found no duplicate. Every citation stays in unit sk-i-curve-zero, there is no cycle, and no tool_uses are needed. Item edge cases J=0, J=S, J=(pi), r=0 and a non-finitely-generated J all hold. No changes were made.
